column6: Snapshot of the E-mini S&P 500 futures price level used as the underlying reference for all option pricing and volatility examples.
Contract size, tick value, trading hours, and expiration cycle used to parameterize futures pricing and PnL calculations.
Option-specific conventions (multiplier, tick size, settlement, exercise style) encoded into option valuation models.
Synthetic options chain reflecting real strike and expiration structure. Prices and implied volatilities are model-generated for illustration.
Select settlement prices used as point-in-time benchmarks for validating pricing models. Full exchange tables are not reproduced.
Exchange reference pricing inputs used to sanity-check model outputs without reproducing calculator interfaces.
Listing and expiration dates used to construct realistic maturity grids for options modeling.
Qualitative observations of volatility term structure and skew used to motivate volatility modeling. No charts or data are reproduced.
Educational tool used solely for visual familiarization with market structure and option chains. No data or screenshots are used in the book.
European-style index options used as a clean benchmark for futures-versus-index validation. Synthetic prices preserve structure without redistributing exchange data.
Scaled Mini-SPX options chain used for size-adjusted comparison against SPX options.
Confirms European exercise, cash settlement, and contract multiplier, removing ambiguity when comparing index and futures options.
